scenario.name: CISA AA24-045A & Cisco Talos — 8Base / Phobos Ransomware: SmokeLoader Delivery, Process Hacker (kprocesshacker.sys) Service Kill & AES-256 Encryption (.8base)
scenario.overview: Imagine a street-level burglary crew that slips into an office through an open desk door or booby-trapped attachment, opens a hidden relay pipe and borrows a signed technician wrench to disable security guards, then climbs past the desk confirmation prompt to tear down the firewall, snap the emergency-recovery levers off the wall, and clamp heavy locks onto every cabinet while popping open a full-screen ransom placard on every desk. In this scenario (T1055, CISA AA24-045A & Cisco Talos - 8Base / Phobos Ransomware: SmokeLoader Delivery, Process Hacker , kprocesshacker.sys Service Kill & AES-256 Encryption .8base), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: smokeLoader / SystemBC SOCKS5 Proxy, then uAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement, then phobos AES-256-CBC Encryption.8base. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering SmokeLoader / SystemBC SOCKS5 Proxy, then UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement, then Phobos AES-256-CBC Encryption.8base, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 6 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 2: UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement (`netsh`) & Shadow Copy / Boot Recovery Wipe
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion & Impact Preparation (T1562.004 - Disable Firewall / T1490)
stages.description: Planting copies of itself inside both the morning startup folder and the master launch registry so it survives reboots, the payload hops past user permission prompts, shuts off the building firewall walls, and cuts off both shadow backups and emergency boot-repair switches. The Phobos/8Base payload copies itself to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup and HKLM\...\Run for persistence, disables the Windows Firewall via netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off, and executes vssadmin, wmic, wbadmin, and bcdedit in a tight loop to prevent system recovery (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with FirewallModification=netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off, RecoveryInhibition=vssadmin + wmic shadowcopy + wbadmin + bcdedit, StartupPersistence=Startup Folder + HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet && wmic.exe shadowcopy delete (which executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet , or WMI Win32_ShadowCopy.Delete to invoke IVssBackupComponents::DeleteSnapshots and purge all exi so that inhibits system recovery , T1562.004 during "UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement , netsh & Shadow Copy / Boot Recovery Wipe" by destroying local disk shadow copies before or after payload execution so defenders cannot roll back encrypted files or inspect historical volume state). Next, the follow-up artifact bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures && bcdedit.exe /set {default} recoveryenabled no runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures && bcdedit.exe /set {default} so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1562.004 during "UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement , netsh & Shadow Copy / Boot Recovery Wipe" , The Phobos/8Base payload copies itself to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup and HKLM\ while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ netsh.exe advfirewall set allprofiles state off / ⇠#2 ACK 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 ProcessHacker.exe (kprocesshacker.sys)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise Shares (.8base + info.hta)).

stages.title: Stage 3: Phobos AES-256-CBC Encryption, `.8base` Extension Rename & `info.hta` HTML Application Note
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact / T1218.005 - Mshta)

Next, the follow-up artifact mshta.exe "C:\Users\Public\info.hta" (Displays HTML Application ransom demand) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , mshta.exe "C:\Users\Public\info.hta" , Displays HTML Application ransom demand via mshta.exe so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1486 during "Phobos AES-256-CBC Encryption.8base Extension Rename & info.hta HTML Application Note" , 8Base encrypts all non-system files using AES-256-CBC , encrypting files under 1 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ phobos_8base.exe / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 ProcessHacker.exe (kprocesshacker.sys)) to Node ④ (#4 Windows Server (vssadmin + bcdedit + firewall off)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise Shares (.8base + info.hta)).

steps.plainTitle: UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement (netsh) & Shadow Copy / Boot Recovery Wipe
steps.storyAnalogy: Planting copies of itself inside both the morning startup folder and the master launch registry so it survives reboots, the payload hops past user permission prompts, shuts off the building firewall walls, and cuts off both shadow backups and emergency boot-repair switches.
steps.simpleExplanation: The Phobos/8Base payload copies itself to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup and HKLM\...\Run for persistence, disables the Windows Firewall via netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off, and executes vssadmin, wmic, wbadmin, and bcdedit in a tight loop to prevent system recovery (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with FirewallModification=netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off, RecoveryInhibition=vssadmin + wmic shadowcopy + wbadmin + bcdedit, StartupPersistence=Startup Folder + HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet && wmic.exe shadowcopy delete (which executes vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet , or WMI Win32_ShadowCopy.Delete to invoke IVssBackupComponents::DeleteSnapshots and purge all exi so that inhibits system recovery , T1562.004 during "UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement , netsh & Shadow Copy / Boot Recovery Wipe" by destroying local disk shadow copies before or after payload execution so defenders cannot roll back encrypted files or inspect historical volume state). Next, the follow-up artifact bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures && bcdedit.exe /set {default} recoveryenabled no runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures && bcdedit.exe /set {default} so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1562.004 during "UAC Bypass, Windows Firewall Disablement , netsh & Shadow Copy / Boot Recovery Wipe" , The Phobos/8Base payload copies itself to %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup and HKLM\ while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).

steps.detectionAndEvidence: Documented in Sysmon Event 1 (recording FirewallModification=netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off, RecoveryInhibition=vssadmin + wmic shadowcopy + wbadmin + bcdedit, StartupPersistence=Startup Folder + HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run under T1562.004): Alert on sequential execution of vssadmin delete shadows, bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no, and netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off within a 5-second window.

steps.plainTitle: Phobos AES-256-CBC Encryption.8base Extension Rename & info.hta HTML Application Note
steps.storyAnalogy: Sweeping across every non-system drawer on the machine, the Phobos locking engine seals small documents completely and seals giant files rapidly in slices, stamps every locked item with an 8base tag, and pops open an interactive ransom placard right on the desktop.
steps.simpleExplanation: 8Base encrypts all non-system files using AES-256-CBC (encrypting files under 1.5 MB completely and larger files partially before protecting the per-victim AES key with an embedded RSA-1024 public key), renames files to <filename>.id[<8_hex_id>].[support@8base.vc].8base, and launches mshta.exe C:\info.hta to display a full-screen extortion notice (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with RansomwareFamily=8Base , Phobos Ransomware-as-a-Service Variant, FilePattern=*.id[<victim_id>].[support@8base.vc].8base, HtmlRansomNote=info.hta launched via mshta.exe so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).

Next, the follow-up artifact mshta.exe "C:\Users\Public\info.hta" (Displays HTML Application ransom demand) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , mshta.exe "C:\Users\Public\info.hta" , Displays HTML Application ransom demand via mshta.exe so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1486 during "Phobos AES-256-CBC Encryption.8base Extension Rename & info.hta HTML Application Note" , 8Base encrypts all non-system files using AES-256-CBC , encrypting files under 1 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
